name: Cursor
look: Warm cream canvas with warm ink, one orange CTA used scarcely, weight-400 magazine display and hairline-only depth.

hero.title: The editor that reads the whole repository
hero.sub: Caret indexes your codebase, understands how the pieces relate, and edits across files the way someone who already knows the project would.

features.title: Context, not autocomplete
features.sub: The difference between a model that has seen your file and one that has read your project.

items.title: Whole-repo index
items.body: Every file embedded and kept current, so a question about one function knows about the three places that call it.

items.title: Multi-file edits
items.body: Describe a refactor and get a reviewable diff across every file it touches, not a snippet to paste.

items.title: Agent mode
items.body: Runs commands, reads the output, and fixes what it broke — with every step shown and revertible.

items.title: Reviewable by default
items.body: Nothing is applied silently. Changes arrive as a diff you accept hunk by hunk.

items.title: Privacy mode
items.body: Code is never stored or trained on. In privacy mode nothing touches disk on our side at all.

items.title: Your extensions
items.body: A fork of the editor you already use, so your themes, keybindings and extensions carry over untouched.

showcases.title: It runs the tests too
showcases.body: Agent mode does not stop at proposing a change. It runs the test suite, reads the failures, and iterates — showing each command and its output, so you can stop it the moment it heads somewhere you did not intend.
points: Every command and its output shown
Stoppable and revertible at any step

showcases.title: Your code stays yours
showcases.body: Privacy mode is enforced at the account level and cannot be overridden by an individual. Code is never persisted on our infrastructure and never used for training, and the SOC 2 report says so in writing.

metric_lead: Measured across the user base this quarter

gallery.title: Documentation
gallery.sub: Getting started, keybindings, the agent protocol and the privacy model.

testimonial.quote: I asked it to move a module and update the callers. It found eleven, including two in a test fixture I had forgotten existed, and showed me the diff before touching anything.
testimonial.name: Ben Aldous

pricing.title: Pricing
pricing.sub: Free to try. Paid plans add the larger models and unlimited agent runs.

items.q: Is my code used for training?
items.a: No. In privacy mode nothing is persisted on our infrastructure at all, and outside it code is used only to answer your request and then discarded. Neither mode contributes to training data.
Yes. Caret is a fork of the editor you already use, so extensions, themes, keybindings and settings carry across on first launch.

items.q: How large a repository can it index?
items.a: Repositories into the millions of lines. Indexing is incremental after the first pass, so day-to-day it keeps up with your branch without noticeable cost.

items.q: Can I use my own API key?
items.a: Yes, on any plan. Bring a key from a supported provider and requests bill to you directly, bypassing our quotas entirely.

cta.title: Try it on a real repository
cta.sub: Free to download, and your extensions and keybindings come with you.

footer.tagline: An editor that has read the whole project.

notes: The canvas is warm cream, not white, and the ink is warm too (#26251e) rather than pure black. That warmth is the entire mood.
One orange CTA, used scarcely. It is the only saturated colour on a marketing page and it appears roughly once per view.
Display type stays at weight 400 — never bold. The voice is magazine, not product launch.
Depth is hairlines only. There are no drop shadows anywhere in this system.
CTA radius is a compact 8px — the developer dialect against an otherwise editorial page.
